# Sales One-Pager & Collateral Design Guide

## Core Rules

- **One page. Non-negotiable.** If it doesn't fit, cut content — not margins or font size.
- **Designed to be left behind or forwarded.** It must work without you in the room.
- **Problem before product.** Open with the buyer's pain, not your logo.
- **Visual hierarchy wins.** Skimmers should get the full story. Readers get the detail.
- **One clear call to action.** Never two.

## One-Pager Structure

### Top Section (above the fold — first thing seen)
- Company logo (top left or center, small)
- Headline: The buyer's problem or the outcome you deliver — not your product name
  - ✅ "Automate SOC triage without losing control of your data"
  - ❌ "Acme Platform Overview"
- Sub-headline: One sentence expanding the value prop (under 20 words)
- Optional: A single striking stat or proof point in large type (e.g., "74% reduction in analyst triage time")

### Middle Section (the proof)
Use 2–3 columns or a clear two-section layout:

**The Problem** (left or top half)
- 3–4 bullet points describing the pain state
- Use buyer's language — the words they'd use to describe their own problem

**The Solution** (right or bottom half)
- 3–4 bullet points on how you solve each pain
- Pair each problem bullet with a solution bullet when possible

**OR** use a "How it works" 3-step visual:
- Step 1 → Step 2 → Step 3 with icons
- Each step: 3–5 words max

### Proof Section
- 2–3 customer logos (if approved) OR one quote with attribution
- One metric per customer if available: "Reduced triage time by 74% — Fortune 500 Insurance Co."
- Keep proof tight — one row, clearly labeled

### Bottom Section
- Feature/capability list (3–6 items max, icon + label format)
- OR a simple comparison table (Us vs. Status Quo — not Us vs. Competitor)
- Call to action: "Schedule a demo at example.com" or "Contact us: sales@example.com"
- QR code optional but useful for physical leave-behinds

## Design Principles for One-Pagers

**Layout:**
- Grid-based: Use columns (2 or 3). Nothing floats randomly.
- Visual weight top-heavy: Most important content in the top third
- Whitespace = credibility. Dense one-pagers feel desperate.

**Typography:**
- Max 2 font styles (e.g., bold for headers, regular for body)
- Headline: 24–36pt
- Section headers: 14–16pt bold
- Body: 10–11pt (minimum for print; 11–12pt for digital)
- Never go below 9pt for anything

**Color:**
- 2–3 colors maximum (background, primary text, 1 accent)
- Accent color on headline, CTA, and key stats only
- High contrast: dark text on white/light, or white text on dark background section

**Icons:**
- Use a consistent icon set (all outline or all filled — never mixed)
- Icons supplement labels; never replace them
- Keep icons small (16–20px equivalent) when used inline

## Vertical-Specific Formatting

**Security / SOC one-pager:**
- Lead with risk reduction and compliance language
- Show workflow: alert → automated triage → approved remediation
- Proof: SOC analyst hours saved, MTTR reduction

**Executive / CRO leave-behind:**
- Pure outcome language — no architecture or technical detail
- 3 boxes: Problem, Outcome, Investment
- One customer quote, one metric, one next step

**Technical / SE-facing datasheet:**
- Architecture diagram (simplified) in center
- Integration list prominently featured
- Deployment model (SaaS vs. self-managed) clearly called out
- Security certifications or compliance badges at bottom
